scope_note: Eleven selected official decision records have individual holding, outcome, procedural posture, applicability, and limitation notes. This selection is not a comprehensive case-law survey; RIS discovery batches remain open.

cases.holding: A NAG §54 residence card documents, with declaratory effect, the directly applicable EU residence right. It does not bind the AMS on a separate AuslBG §3(8) certificate question. The BVwG also failed to assess the card and the requested oral hearing.
cases.outcome: Revision allowed; the BVwG decision was set aside for substantive legal error.
cases.procedural_posture: Extraordinary revision from the BVwG after the AMS refused an AuslBG §3(8) certificate.
cases.applicability: Useful for the evidentiary effect of a residence card and for keeping the immigration documentation question distinct from the separate labour-market certificate procedure.
cases.limits: It does not decide a visa application or the NAG §55(3) continued-residence route.

cases.holding: On the evidence before it, the court did not accept the authority’s sham-marriage finding under NAG §54(7) and accepted a genuine shared family life.
cases.outcome: Appeal allowed; authority decision set aside.
cases.procedural_posture: Complaint from the administrative finding/refusal; administrative-court review.
cases.applicability: Shows why the specific §54(7) factual ground and evidence must be tested.
cases.limits: Fact-specific; does not establish a general burden-of-proof rule or broaden statutory family-member categories.

cases.holding: A residence card has declaratory effect. NAG §37(4) suspends the VwGVG §8 delay-complaint period while the specified investigation is pending; once the suspension ends, the authority must take further steps without delay to avoid remaining in default.
cases.outcome: Revision allowed; the Verwaltungsgericht Wien decision was set aside for substantive legal error.
cases.procedural_posture: Revision in a delay proceeding concerning issuance of a non-decision-form residence-card document.
cases.applicability: Relevant to delay challenges and to the relationship between the NAG investigation period and the VwGVG delay route.
cases.limits: The decision remitted the particular delay matter; its timing analysis must be applied to the procedural facts and the exact statutory version.

cases.holding: Where EU residence rights may have ceased, a person already issued EU residence documentation remains lawfully present under FPG §31(1)(2) until completion of the NAG §55 procedure. That domestic-law lawful stay does not itself establish entitlement to an AuslBG §3(8) certificate; the separate employment-law conditions still require findings.
cases.outcome: Revision allowed; the BVwG decision was set aside for substantive legal error and missing findings.
cases.procedural_posture: Ordinary revision from the BVwG in a labour-market certificate proceeding involving an EU-family residence document and a downstream NAG status issue.
cases.applicability: Maps the interim lawful-stay consequence while §55 is pending and prevents conflating lawful stay with labour-market eligibility.
cases.limits: The case is not a general holding that every person with an expired or questioned card has an EU right.

cases.holding: NAG §54(7) can apply to an application based on a sham marriage even if that marriage has already ended by the time of decision. The court nevertheless had to make a reasonable effort to hear the proposed witness using known Hungarian addresses; its refusal to pursue that evidence was inadequately reasoned.
cases.outcome: Revision allowed; the Verwaltungsgericht Wien decision was set aside for a material procedural error.
cases.procedural_posture: Ordinary revision from a Vienna administrative-court decision affirming sham-marriage findings and rejecting residence-card applications.
cases.applicability: Directly relevant to the scope of §54(7) and the evidence/procedure required before a sham-marriage conclusion.
cases.limits: The judgment does not make divorce proof of abuse or dispense with individualized evidence and procedural fairness.

cases.holding: A court may assess whether the EU-derived residence right existed even while a residence card remains current; the card is declaratory and does not foreclose that substantive inquiry. The decision concerns entitlement to permanent residence and a suspected sham marriage, and discusses the retained right following divorce.
cases.outcome: Revision allowed; the Verwaltungsgericht Wien decision was set aside for substantive legal error.
cases.procedural_posture: Ordinary revision in a residence-card/permanent-residence dispute following a sham-marriage finding.
cases.applicability: Relevant to whether an unexpired card conclusively proves a continuing or permanent EU right, and to the limited role of §55(3) where the existence of the claimed right itself is contested.
cases.limits: Its procedural setting and permanent-residence issue matter; it should not be generalized to bypass the distinct NAG §54(7) and §55(3) routes.

cases.holding: An Iranian spouse of an Austrian citizen did not qualify under NAG §57 because the sponsor had not returned to Austria non-temporarily after exercising free movement; the couple continued to live abroad.
cases.outcome: Complaint dismissed as unfounded; ordinary revision inadmissible.
cases.procedural_posture: Complaint from refusal of a residence card under NAG §§54 and 57 after an oral hearing.
cases.applicability: Illustrates the returned-Austrian/free-movement condition on these facts.
cases.limits: Does not decide a case where the sponsor actually returned to Austria or whether another national/EU route applies.

cases.holding: Distinguishes the §54(7) exclusion from ordinary §55(3) continued-right assessment and downstream FPG §§66/70(3) measures.
cases.outcome: Complaints dismissed; one-month deferment; revision not allowed. VwGH later refused related revisions Ro 2023/22/0090–0091 on 27 July 2026; capture of that follow-up remains pending.
cases.procedural_posture: BVwG review of BFA decisions concerning family-member removal/expulsion after residence-right questions.
cases.applicability: Useful as a procedural-sequence example and for the §54(7)/§55(3) distinction.
cases.limits: Fact-dependent; later VwGH follow-up and current FPG/BFA-VG text must be checked before application.

cases.holding: NAG §55(3) is procedural and applies to the administrative court through VwGVG §17. Except for the distinct §54(7) route, a court may not deny the residence-card application on §54 conditions without the §55(3) process; BFA assessment is a preliminary question.
cases.outcome: Revision allowed; challenged judgment set aside.
cases.procedural_posture: Revision from an administrative-court decision concerning residence-card rights, after delay/jurisdiction transfer.
cases.limits: Read with the full judgment and current law; arose from a specific family and procedural posture.

cases.holding: Reviewed a BFA decision following NAG §55(3), involving FPG §66 and §70(3), after divorce before three years of marriage; the court upheld the measure on the facts.
cases.outcome: Complaint dismissed as unfounded; ordinary revision inadmissible.
cases.procedural_posture: BVwG merits review of a BFA removal/expulsion-related decision with a one-month deferment.
cases.applicability: Recent example connecting continued-right assessment to downstream FPG procedure.
cases.limits: Does not establish that every divorce before three years leads to expulsion; FPG and BFA-VG provisions still require independent current-text review.

cases.holding: The VwGH found no question of fundamental significance. The underlying matter involved expulsion under FPG §66 together with NAG §55(3), and dependent adult relatives under NAG §52(1)(3); the Court treated the CJEU C-423/12 dependency-in-country-of-origin issue as settled and found the procedural objections lacked a sufficient relevance showing.
cases.outcome: Revisions rejected as inadmissible; the BVwG outcomes remained in place.
cases.procedural_posture: Extraordinary revisions from two BVwG decisions, W112 2246196-2/33E and W112 2246194-2/40E, concerning expulsion of Russian nationals.
cases.applicability: A follow-up review point for the paired BVwG decisions and a current confirmation that this record is a refusal of revision, not a new merits holding on §54(7) or §55(3).
cases.limits: Do not cite the VwGH refusal as substantive precedent resolving the underlying residence or removal merits.
